speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing, and how long they typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Does the patient have any history of head trauma, recent infections, or a family history of seizures?
I will also request an EEG to evaluate for abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste and right-sided EEG findings strongly suggest focal seizures originating in the right temporal lobe, likely involving the insula. To help rule out structural causes, have you noticed any other neurological deficits, or is there any family history of epilepsy or specific genetic syndromes? REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRI and right temporal EEG findings, I suspect autoimmune encephalitis, particularly anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis. Has the patient exhibited any psychiatric symptoms, speech abnormalities, or autonomic instability in the weeks preceding these episodes?

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste (gustatory aura) and right temporal EEG findings are classic for focal seizures, likely originating in the insula or mesial temporal lobe, rather than autoimmune encephalitis which typically presents with more systemic or psychiatric symptoms. Do the episodes occur exclusively during sleep, or do they happen during waking hours as well?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRI, right temporal EEG spikes, and gustatory aura, this presentation is highly consistent with temporal lobe epilepsy. Are the episodes occurring exclusively during sleep, or do they also happen while he is awake?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, headache, visual or auditory disturbances, weakness, or other systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the episodes occur exclusively during sleep, or do they also happen while he is awake? DIAGNOSIS READY: Focal Epilepsy (Temporal Lobe Epilepsy)
